units.en: As ⟦0⟧, own and control the state of Bourgogne.
⟦0⟧ must be disabled for this strategy to work. Otherwise, ⟦1⟧ will not invite you to join the ⟦2⟧.
At the start of the game choose one state with 2 levels of ⟦0⟧ and prioritise upgrading it to level 3. Delete your army.
Go down the ⟦0⟧ side of the tree and choose to ⟦1⟧.
Don't spend any ⟦0⟧ until you reach ⟦1⟧ and spend it all on the decisions it unlocks.
The focus ⟦0⟧ will allow you reach level 3 of the revolution decisions and spawns a couple divisions in the states you maxed.

If done correctly you should be able to launch the civil war and be ⟦0⟧ by the end of 1936. After that build up your industry (both the communist and economy sub-trees give a good number of factories).
Justify a war goal and declare war on ⟦0⟧. Annex them completely in the peace deal.

Have 2 divisions sit on the Faroe Islands and Jan Mayen each. Also build up 2 ⟦0⟧ and 2 ⟦1⟧ on each island. These two provinces must be held to form the Kalmar Union, and you do not want to lose them to a naval invasion. Greenland is not required, but if you want to garrison it with 2 divisions as well, that's not a bad idea. It is an easy naval invasion point for Canada later if you end up needing it later. Alternatively, you can release Greenland as a puppet and just not call them into your future wars until you need them for a naval invasion.

Continue building your army and economy and prepare a war goal for ⟦0⟧ to use in August or early September 1939.

When ⟦0⟧ declares war do the same. A couple in-game hours later ⟦1⟧ will allow you to join the ⟦2⟧. If you miss the timing and your justification will not finish until mid-October 1939 or later, cancel it. Instead, wait for Germany to declare on Poland. Afterwards, World Tension will wildly spike, and you can directly justify a war goal on the UK in 40 days. As long as you are at war with the Allies before January 1940, you should be asked to join the Axis. Otherwise, at any time past then, Germany will often declare war on you.

If you miss the timing and your justification will not finish until mid-October 1939 or later, cancel it. Instead, wait for ⟦0⟧ to declare on ⟦1⟧. Afterwards, World Tension will wildly spike, and you can directly justify a war goal on the ⟦2⟧ in 40 days.
As long as you are at war with the ⟦0⟧ before January 1940, you should be asked to join the ⟦1⟧. Otherwise, at any time past then, ⟦2⟧ will often declare war on you.
Together, defeat ⟦0⟧, the Benelux countries, and ⟦1⟧.

Declare war on ⟦0⟧. Afterwards, you should be able to form the ⟦1⟧ (as long as you didn't lose anything), even while being at war. This will skyrocket your manpower and factory count. Tip for making this war easy: don't put any troops on Copenhagen (only attack from the Norway side and put a couple divisions on Fyn to protect the rest of Denmark). For some reason, the AI loves to send half of its army to stand on Copenhagen, and you can just take most of their victory points without much hassle. You'll also fully encircle half of their army this way (once you take the Swedish side of the strait), and you can wipe the stack out to get a ton of war participation, which you will need.

In the peace deal take Bourgogne and if you're going for ⟦0⟧ after, also take ⟦1⟧ (to form the ⟦2⟧ - also don't forget the Isle of Man) and try to get the states in Eastern ⟦3⟧ that border the ⟦4⟧. After that focus on spending the remainder of your points on the ⟦5⟧ Fleet.

*After ⟦0⟧'s buff to the ⟦1⟧ AI, this strategy does still work with some alterations. You will need to either heavily focus on a naval build-up (to get Naval Dominance to naval invade, you're going to have to beat the Royal Navy yourself) or an air build-up (to beat the Royal Air Force so badly you get Air Superiority over the Home Islands and can launch a paradrop) alongside your army. You also will very likely not finish the ⟦2⟧ before the ⟦3⟧ joins the ⟦4⟧, which means you won't be seeing a peace conference for a long time (and you'll probably get this achievement and ⟦5⟧ at the same time even if you weren't trying to).

If you are going the naval route, build up Dockyards until you have a minimum of 40. You can get a little over 10 Dockyards for free via Focuses as well. Take advantage of the Convoys to Destroyers En Masse decision, which allows you to infinitely trade 40 Convoys for 10 Destroyers. You'll also need probably a minimum of ~20 Basic or Improved Light Cruisers filled out with Medium Battery and Secondary Turret modules (and Armor II) in addition to all the free destroyers you get (which are mainly there just to soak damage because they're awful). Your first engagement with the Royal Navy will probably be a wash - you'll lose a ton of the free destroyers and a small handful of Light Cruisers, while they will lose around 70-90% of their screens. That's fine. Go back and repair. In the next fight, you should basically wipe out the entire half of the Royal Navy that's assigned to defend the ⟦0⟧. This happens because without all those screens you destroyed in the first battle, their capital ships will be vulnerable to your crazy high Light Attack stats and they'll lose very badly.

As for the air route, just rush for Improved Small Airframe and Engine III in mid-1939, design a Fighter with those and 3 of 4x Heavy Machine Gun, Self-Sealing Fuel Tank, Armor Plates, and Drop Tanks. Put at least 15 factories on this, cutting Infantry Equipment if you need. You'll need to immediately rush for Synthetic Refineries as well (and build at least 15-20 of them) in order to solve your ⟦0⟧ and fuel shortages. Get some 30-width Paratrooper divisions out (you'll have to build out your ground forces so you can make more than a couple of these) and take the doctrine to cause organization drops when paradropping. Build transport planes to carry them as well, of course. Launch a paradrop onto a ⟦1⟧ port from the airport at Calais, hitting Force Attack right as they leave. Once they win, immediately send your armies to join them. Some will die or lose loads of strength to submarine attacks, but that's fine. You should still have more than enough to secure a solid foothold and take the Isles.

Neither route is "better", there's trade-offs to both. Naval will take you longer because realistically you probably won't be able to take the Royal Navy in a fight before 1943 safely (depends slightly on how many Dockyards you build), but you can paradrop as early as mid-1941 if you're doing it right. The advantage of the naval route is that you can stop all of the convoy raiding and actually trade with other countries and consistently supply your troops. Having a strong airforce will make pushing through the ⟦0⟧ much easier after adding in some CAS, but getting a landing point in the Americas can be hard. Sometimes, ⟦1⟧ will still be alive and will have joined the ⟦2⟧ (they join in 1941 or 1942 and often hold out well against naval invasions because of the terrain). You can use them to paradrop into ⟦3⟧ and start your invasion of North America.
